# Refactor-Safety Gate: `apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/services/lifecycle.py`

Scope of this phase: measure whether this module's behaviour is pinned well
enough to refactor. No code or tests were modified. No module split is
proposed here.

## 1. Measurement (real output, run twice, from repo root)

Environment note: `/home/agent` is a small tmpfs and the default `uv` cache
lives there, which caused the first attempt to fail with `No space left on
device` while extracting `pyright`. Redirecting `UV_CACHE_DIR` to a directory
on the larger overlay filesystem fixed it. This is an environment quirk of
this sandbox, not a repo issue, but it's the kind of thing that makes a
coverage run "fail silently into looking fine" if you don't read the warning
text, so it's recorded here.

Run 1 — restricted to the three files that reference `lifecycle` by name:

```
UV_CACHE_DIR=/workspace/.uv-cache uv run pytest -m unit \
  --cov=syn_api.services.lifecycle --cov-report=term-missing -q \
  -k "lifecycle or capture_posture or execution_concurrency_posture"
```

Run 2 — the entire `syn-api` unit suite, no keyword filter, to check whether
any other test touches this module incidentally (e.g. through app import or
a shared fixture):

```
UV_CACHE_DIR=/workspace/.uv-cache uv run pytest apps/syn-api/tests -m unit \
  --cov=syn_api.services.lifecycle --cov-report=term-missing -q
```

Both runs produced **the identical number**:

```
Name                                             Stmts   Miss Branch BrPart  Cover   Missing
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
apps/syn-api/src/syn_api/services/lifecycle.py     345    235     84      2    28%   57-61, 166-169, 179-197, 228, 246-247,
252-268, 277-301, 310-319, 333-343, 472-479, 497-510, 520-539, 544-561, 573-577, 582-586, 591-595, 603-614, 623-630,
639-652, 657-662, 670-735, 740-742, 751-784, 789-791, 853, 858, 863, 868-873, 878-884, 894-907
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
TOTAL                                              345    235     84      2    28%
```

**28% line coverage, 84 branches with only 2 partially covered.** The
identical result across "just the relevant-looking files" and "the entire
unit suite" is itself a finding: nothing else in the codebase exercises this
module, directly or through a fixture, app-lifespan, or `/health` call.

## 2. Coverage per unit, not per file

The file-level number hides a hard split. Two small, pure "diagnostics"
functions account for almost the entire covered 28%; the module's actual
reason for existing — the ADR-057 declarative service registry (init,
recovery, shutdown) — is **at 0%**.

| Unit | Lines | Status | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| `_validate_workspace_settings` | 133-155 | **Covered** | Direct tests, all branches |
| `_log_execution_concurrency_posture` | 349-377 | **Covered** | Direct tests, both branches |
| `_log_session_capture_posture` | 380-459 | **Covered** | Direct tests, extensive, all branches incl. hostile-input cases |
| `startup()` — diagnostics prologue (credentials skip, posture logging, own try/except) | 220-247 | **Partially covered** | Missing: 228 (`validate_credentials` call — never exercised since tests always pass `skip_validation=True`), 246-247 (the concurrency-posture's own `except` — nothing makes that call raise in any test, unlike its capture-posture sibling which is deliberately made to raise) |
| `startup()` — everything past the `is_test` early return | 252-268 | **0% covered** | Offline seeding branch, `_init_critical_path`, `_init_durable_stores`, `_init_degradable_services`, final mode computation — none of it runs, because every test in this repo sets `APP_ENVIRONMENT=test` (see §4) |
| `_handle_recovery_task_exception` | 55-65 | **0% covered** | The only place a crashed recovery task's exception is ever logged |
| `_init_critical_path` | 158-169 | **0% covered** (body) | The "ordering" test asserts on `inspect.getsource()` text — see §3 |
| `_init_degradable_services` | 172-197 | **0% covered** | The registry loop itself: iterate, catch, mark degraded, reconcile orphans, spawn recovery task |
| `shutdown()` | 271-301 | **0% covered** | Never invoked at all — no test drives the FastAPI lifespan's shutdown phase (see §4) |
| `health_check()` | 304-319 | **0% covered** (body) | Never called by any test; the `def` line shows as "covered" only because importing the module executes it — this is exactly the def-line vs. body-execution trap described in §3 |
| `_enrich_codex_auth_health` | 322-343 | **0% covered** (body) | Codex-credential freshness probe never exercised |
| `_enrich_subscription_health` | 542-561 | **0% covered** | Subscription-degraded-mode logic, including the branch that flips `mode` from `"full"` back to `"degraded"` |
| `_init_durable_stores` | 462-479 | **0% covered** | DB pool init + delegate ledger dependency ordering |
| `_init_import_ledger` | 482-510 | **0% covered** | The one CRITICAL (abort-on-failure) service besides the event store |
| `_init_event_store` | 513-539 | **0% covered** | **The single most important function in the file** — the only unconditionally-critical startup dependency — has zero direct test |
| `_init_artifact_storage` / `_init_claude_plugin_storage` / `_init_skill_storage` | 571-595 | **0% covered** | All three MinIO bucket `ensure_ready()` calls |
| `_init_conversation_storage` / `_shutdown_conversation_storage` | 598-630 | **0% covered** | Including the singleton-reset-on-retry logic |
| `_init_subscriptions` / `_shutdown_subscriptions` | 633-662 | **0% covered** | Including the "reuse existing dispatcher across recovery attempts" logic |
| `_init_event_poller` / `_shutdown_event_poller` | 665-742 | **0% covered** | Largest uncovered block. Every branch: GitHub-not-configured, polling-disabled, cursor-store-from-DB, cursor-store-unavailable-in-production (refuses to start the poller), in-memory-cursor-fallback (test/offline only) |
| `_init_check_run_poller` / `_shutdown_check_run_poller` | 745-791 | **0% covered** | Same shape as the event poller, plus the `add_observer` wiring |
| `_is_recoverable` / `_get_recoverable` / `_all_recovered` | 851-863 | **0% covered** | Pure predicates over the registry — trivial to test, currently untested |
| `_try_recover_reason` / `_attempt_recovery_pass` / `_recovery_loop` | 866-907 | **0% covered** | The entire background recovery loop: backoff schedule (10s → 60s cap, doubling), shutdown-cancellation race, exit-when-all-recovered condition |

Net: **every function that touches real infrastructure — event store, DB
pool, object storage, conversation storage, subscription coordinator, GitHub
pollers, and the recovery loop that stitches them together — is at 0%.**
The covered 28% is exclusively the two logging/diagnostics helpers and one
settings-validation gate, none of which touch `_SERVICE_REGISTRY` at all.

## 3. Coverage vs. assertion — read, not assumed

I read all three test files that reference this module in full
(`test_lifecycle_workspace_settings_gate.py`, `test_capture_posture.py`,
`test_execution_concurrency_posture.py`, 362 lines total).

**The covered 28% is genuinely behaviour-pinned, not just executed.** These
are unusually strong tests for the surface they touch:

- They assert on message *content*, not just log level or "no exception
  raised" — e.g. `test_no_url_shaped_value_reaches_a_record` parametrizes
  nine ways a secret could leak into a log line (userinfo, query string,
  path segment, fragment, bare token-as-host, scheme, brackets) and checks
  the token appears in none of `record.getMessage()`, `record.args`, or the
  raw input.
- Several docstrings/comments name a *specific prior bug or mutation* the
  test now guards against — e.g. "An earlier version asserted
  `syntropic137__dev`, a value no deployment produces," or "a codex mutation
  that appended `store.url.rsplit('/')[-1]` to the destination passed the
  entire suite." That is mutation-tested language, the strongest signal that
  a test pins behaviour rather than merely running a line.
- `TestOnePostureCannotSuppressTheOther` deliberately makes one diagnostic
  raise and asserts the *other* diagnostic still fires — a genuine
  regression test for a specific coupling bug, exercised through
  `lifecycle.startup()` itself (with `skip_validation=True`), not just the
  helper in isolation.

**One test in this set does not execute anything and should not be read as
coverage of the code it names.**
`test_the_gate_runs_before_degradable_services` in
`test_lifecycle_workspace_settings_gate.py` does this:

```python
source = inspect.getsource(lifecycle)
gate = source.index("await _init_critical_path()")
degradable = source.index("await _init_degradable_services(")
assert gate < degradable
```

This is a text-position assertion on the module's source string. It proves
the two call sites appear in the right *textual* order; it proves nothing
about runtime behaviour, and it would stay green even if `startup()`'s
actual control flow were changed to call them in the other order through
some indirection (a helper, a conditional, a different code path) as long as
the literal substrings still appeared in that order somewhere in the file.
Coverage tooling correctly reports 0% for both functions' bodies despite
this test existing — the numbers and the test agree here, which is worth
noting since it's easy for a check like this to *feel* like it tested
ordering while the coverage tool quietly disagrees.

**A second, structural trap in the raw numbers:** a function's `def` line
(and any bare docstring statement) is marked "covered" the moment the module
is *imported*, regardless of whether the function is ever called. `def
health_check():` at line 304 imports as covered; its body (310-319) does
not, because nothing calls it. Anyone skimming coverage by file percentage
rather than by line range would credit `health_check` with partial coverage
it doesn't have. This is why §2 reports per-function, not per-file.

## 4. Why the 0% is this total: `APP_ENVIRONMENT=test` is global

`conftest.py` at the repo root sets `os.environ["APP_ENVIRONMENT"] = "test"`
before any other import, and it is not overridden by any test that touches
this module. `startup()` checks `settings.is_test` and returns
`Ok({"mode": "full"})` immediately (line 249-250) — before the critical path,
before durable-store init, before the entire service registry ever runs.
Every test in this repo therefore only ever exercises the first ~30 lines of
`startup()`.

Separately, `shutdown()` is wired as the FastAPI `lifespan` shutdown handler
in `main.py`, but no test in this repo constructs the app with a triggered
lifespan (`with TestClient(app):` or `httpx.ASGITransport(..., lifespan=...)`)
— the two tests that do build an ASGI client use bare `AsyncClient` /
`ASGITransport` without opting into lifespan events. `shutdown()` is
consequently invoked zero times across the entire suite, confirmed by two
independent coverage runs against different test selections returning the
exact same 0% for lines 277-301.

## 5. Module boundaries — what a refactor must preserve exactly

**Reads:** `get_settings()` (multiple fields: `is_test`, `is_offline`,
`uses_in_memory_stores`, `session_store`, `polling.*`, `github.is_configured`,
`codex_auth_json`, `app_environment`), `WorkspaceSettings()`.

**Calls out to (via `syn_api._wiring` and adjacent adapters/services):**
`get_event_store_instance`, `ensure_connected`, `disconnect`,
`get_realtime`, `get_subscription_coordinator`, `get_workflow_dispatcher`,
`validate_credentials`, `reconcile_orphaned_sessions`,
`cleanup_orphaned_containers`, `seed_offline_data`,
`get_artifact_storage`/`get_claude_plugin_storage`/`get_skill_storage`
(each `.ensure_ready()`), `get_conversation_storage`/
`reset_conversation_storage`, `init_shared_db_pool`/`get_shared_db_pool`/
`close_shared_db_pool`, `_create_import_ledger`, GitHub adapters
(`get_github_client`, `GitHubEventsAPIClient`, `GitHubChecksAPIClient`,
`GitHubRepoIngestionService`, `GitHubEventIngestionScheduler`,
`CheckRunIngestionService`), poller-cursor stores (Postgres/in-memory),
`get_event_pipeline`, `get_trigger_store`, `get_webhook_health_tracker`,
`get_pending_sha_store`, `describe_codex_auth`, `deployment_identity`.

**Mutates:** the module-level singleton `_state: LifecycleState`
(`subscription_service`, `workflow_dispatcher`, `event_poller`,
`check_run_poller`, `conversation_storage`, `degraded_reasons`,
`_recovery_task`, `_shutting_down`) — this is genuine hidden module state,
not passed explicitly, and every `_init_*`/`_shutdown_*` function reads or
writes it.

**Spawns:** a background `asyncio.Task` (`_recovery_loop`) with backoff
timing that is itself untested, plus a `done_callback` for exception
logging.

**Public contract consumed elsewhere:** `startup()`, `shutdown()`,
`health_check()` — called from `main.py`'s FastAPI `lifespan`. `startup()`'s
`Result[dict, LifecycleError]` shape (`mode`, `degraded_reasons`) and
`health_check()`'s response dict shape are both externally observed (e.g. by
an npx setup wizard per the module's own docstring comments) and must not
change incidentally during a refactor.

Every one of these boundaries — registry iteration order (init forward,
shutdown reverse), the critical-vs-degradable failure contract (`Err` aborts
startup vs. logged-and-appended-to-`degraded_reasons`), the recovery loop's
backoff/exit conditions, and the "no secret ever reaches a log record"
invariant on the two posture functions — is exactly the kind of thing a
structural refactor silently breaks, and right now only the last one has a
test that would catch it.

## 6. Existing test files for this module

- `apps/syn-api/tests/test_lifecycle_workspace_settings_gate.py`
- `apps/syn-api/tests/test_capture_posture.py`
- `apps/syn-api/tests/test_execution_concurrency_posture.py`

No other file in `apps/`, `packages/`, or the submodules references this
module, its public functions, or `_SERVICE_REGISTRY` (verified by
whole-tree grep and corroborated by the two identical coverage runs).

---

# VERDICT: CHARACTERIZATION TESTS REQUIRED FIRST

This is the expected, successful outcome for a 907-line module whose
covered 28% happens to be its two logging helpers and one validation gate,
while its architectural centerpiece — a declarative service registry that
the module's own docstring describes as the reason the file is shaped the
way it is — sits at a measured, reproducible 0%.

**What is actually pinned today, with confidence:** `_validate_workspace_settings`,
`_log_execution_concurrency_posture`, and `_log_session_capture_posture` are
well-tested by assertions that check message content and specific historical
regressions, not just line execution or exception absence. A refactor that
only touches these three functions, keeping their signatures and observable
logging/return behaviour, is low-risk today.

**What is not pinned at all, and must be before any structural change:**
`startup()`'s non-test-mode path (critical path, durable stores, degradable
services), `shutdown()` in its entirety, `health_check()`'s enrichment
functions, every individual `_init_*`/`_shutdown_*` service function, and the
recovery loop. These are not "thin coverage" — they are unexercised. A
refactor here is a rewrite with hope attached, per the framing of this task:
nothing today would fail if the registry-iteration order were silently
reversed, if a service's exception stopped being caught, if the recovery
backoff stopped doubling, or if `shutdown()` stopped closing the DB pool.

**Residual risk even after characterization tests are added:** this module's
side effects are inherently about real infrastructure (Docker-adjacent
storage backends, DB pools, GitHub API clients, a subscription coordinator).
Characterization tests here will necessarily be test-doubles/mocks around
`syn_api._wiring` factory functions rather than true black-box behavioural
tests — which pins *this module's* orchestration logic (ordering, error
handling, state mutation) correctly, but cannot by itself prove the
composed system still boots. That gap should be closed with the recorded
integration/e2e tiers this repo already has (per `AGENTS.md`'s testing
section), not by inflating unit-test scope to fake an end-to-end guarantee.
